title.narrative: Development and adoption of appropriate technologies for enhancing productivity in the cement sector

description.narrative: The project has been developed in response to a request from the Government of India dated 19 September 2014. The overall objective of this project is to strengthen the capacity of the National Council for Cement and Building Materials (NCCBM), who will in turn act as a key support institution in strengthening the global competitive position of the Indian cement sector. India's cement industry is a vital part of its economy, providing employment to more than a million people, directly or indirectly. Cement production in India is a fragmented industry with more than 500 players. However, the sector is rather oligopolistic in nature as the top 10 producers control about 70% of the domestic market. The recent slowdown in demand has negatively affected the sector but small producers experienced the biggest reduction in capacity utilisation. Ever since it was deregulated in 1982, the Indian cement industry has attracted huge investments, from both Indian and foreign investors, making it the second largest in the world, accounting for about 7% of the global production. Since cement is a cyclical commodity, the dynamics of production are highly dependent on the overall economic activity in India.
